newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Tietmeyer says no deal yet on German reserves.
newsitem.headline: Tietmeyer says no deal yet on German reserves.

text.p: Bundesbank President Hans Tietmeyer said no deal had been struck yet on Bonn's plans to revalue the central bank's official reserves, but that talks were continuing.
Speaking to reporters, Tietmeyer said, "We have had only a talk, but of course no deal and the discussion is going on."
Tietmeyer made the comments as he arrived in Interlaken at an the International Monetary Conference.

Earlier in the day, German Finance Minister Theo Waigel told journalists he and Tietmeyer had reached "a good compromise" on his controversial plan to revalue the central bank's assets and reap a windfall profit for the government.
Under terms of the compromise as presented by the government, the Bundesbank would revalue its gold and currency reserves this year, but not make any profit transfer to Bonn until 1998.
The Finance Ministry had orignally hoped to have profits from the asset revalution transfered to Bonn this year to help it cut the budget deficit and qualify for European monetary union.
The Bundesbank rejected the plan, however, saying the scheme amounted to an attack on its independence and that it would damage confidence in the euro.
Bonn is fighting to reduce its budget deifict to three percent of gross domestic product by the end of the year in order to qualify for European monetary union.
But sluggish economic growth and unemployment payments have made cutting government red ink difficult, forcing Waigel to search for other sources of revenue.
